manifest.title: Orbit
manifest.author: Marcus Quinn <marcus@marcusquinn.com>
manifest.description:
Orbit is a self-hosted workspace for teams: tasks, docs and chat in one app on
your own server. AI clients connect over MCP and work with the whole workspace
without your data leaving the server.

### Features

* **Tasks:** projects with custom workflows; list, board and timeline views;
  sub-issues, labels, saved views and trash. GitHub sync, and import from
  Asana, Linear and Trello.
* **Docs:** a page tree with live collaborative editing, version history,
  search and Notion import.
* **Chat:** channels, direct messages, threads, files and search.
* **AI:** an MCP server with OAuth. AI clients can read and write tasks and
  docs, and read chat.
* **Admin:** workspaces, members, roles, API tokens, audit log, email, sign-in
  providers, rate limits, storage and workspace export.
* **Sign-in:** email and password or passkeys; Google and GitHub sign-in are
  optional.

Orbit's Mail section is still in development upstream and shows "Coming soon";
it is not a working mail client yet.

### Cloudron integration

* **Backups:** the SQLite database (backed up consistently), attachments and
  the app key are in Cloudron backups.
* **Outgoing mail:** invitations, password resets and sign-up links can go
  through the Cloudron mail relay. Run `orbit-mail-settings` in the Terminal
  for the values to enter in Orbit's Admin → Email page.
* **Command line:** `orbit`, `orbit-offline` and `orbit-setup-link` in the
  Terminal run the upstream operator CLI with this app's settings.

Cloudron single sign-on is not available: Orbit does not support OpenID
Connect yet.

[Orbit](https://github.com/coollabsio/orbit) is open source under the
Apache-2.0 licence. This package is maintained independently of the Orbit
project.
manifest.tagline: Self-hosted tasks, docs and team chat in one workspace
manifest.postInstallMessage:
**Create the root account.** When Orbit first starts it prints a one-time
setup link in the app's **Logs**. Open it to create the root account and your
first workspace. For a fresh link, run `orbit-setup-link` in the app's
**Terminal**. Treat the link as a password: whoever opens it first becomes the
root user.

**Set up email** in Orbit's **Admin → Email** page. Orbit needs it for
password resets, email changes, emailed invitations and open registration. Run
`orbit-mail-settings` in the Terminal for the Cloudron mail relay's values (the
output includes the relay password), choose **None (local relay only)** as the
encryption, save, and use **Send test email**. Run it again if mail stops after
the app's email settings change or the app is cloned.

**Invite your team** from **Settings → Members**. **Generate link** works
without email. Registration stays closed unless you open it in
**Admin → General**.

Keep backups of the app: `/app/data/secrets/app-key` decrypts the mail and
sign-in provider secrets Orbit stores.

Settings and commands: [README](https://github.com/marcusquinn/cloudron-orbit-app/blob/main/README.md).
manifest.changelog:
* Initial Cloudron package for Orbit 0.2.1 (upstream commit fe9dce7), built from upstream's release image pinned by digest.
* SQLite database, attachments and the app key in /app/data, with Cloudron's consistent SQLite backups.
* Outgoing mail through the Cloudron relay: `orbit-mail-settings` prints the values for Admin → Email.
* `orbit-setup-link` prints a fresh first-run setup link; `orbit-offline` runs the upstream CLI commands that need the server stopped.
* Orbit's Mail section is still a preview with mock data upstream.
